about: Recorded demo data for Module 4 (MGMT 615, fictional). 'activities' are the module's activities after the refresh review. Each has type, title, CLOs, weight (high, medium, low), estimated student hours, RSI category (null if it doesn't count on its own) and AI-completion risk for graded work. 'review' holds the refresh findings for steps 4.1 and 4.2. Activities from the course map are kept unless a finding says otherwise.

activities.title: Introductions and Your Management Story
Case Analysis: Maria's First Ninety Days and Dana's First Bad Week
Manager vs. Individual Contributor Sort

review: Case analysis: keep, and add Dana's first bad week as the comparison case so the assignment sits at the storyline's first decision.
The sort is auto-graded, so it doesn't count for RSI. The module still has two categories from the discussion and the case feedback.
About 4.5 hours of activities in a 4-hour first week. Resolution: the Manager vs. Individual Contributor Sort becomes optional practice, and the case analysis is shortened.

review: Motivation memo: tie it to Dana's bonus decision. It was a general memo on a problem of the student's choice; students can still add their own team as a second case.

review: Perusall now counts for RSI (category 4) with the Thursday replies planned in step 2.2.

review: The memo used a separate case, The Team That Couldn't Ship. Keep that case as a reading and move the memo to Dana's handoff decision, which the Module 4 scenario plan already sets up.

review: Two high-stakes assignments in the last week, about 6 hours before readings and the cohort session. Consider moving the Management Approach Summary's first draft into Module 7 or shortening it.

aiCheck.why: A general AI tool writes a plausible SBI feedback script from the scenario alone, with no student judgment visible.
aiCheck.change: Students annotate their own script with why each line is there, and rehearse it with a partner in the cohort session. The annotations and the rehearsal are graded.

aiCheck.why: Drafting an announcement from a brief is a strength of AI tools.
aiCheck.change: Grade the resistance map first and require the message to answer each mapped source of resistance, then hold a table read in the cohort session where classmates play the crew.

aiCheck.why: A general reflection on management approach can be produced without the course.
aiCheck.change: Students build it from their own earlier submissions, quoting at least three of them and saying what they would now do differently.

aiCheck.why: AI can apply expectancy theory to the bonus case, but the second case from the student's own team needs their knowledge.
aiCheck.change: Keep the student's own team as a required second case.
